summary: Valleyview Provincial Park lookout in the Annapolis area, on a 2009 DNR list; province-wide decommissioning in 2015 per CBC; no source ties the tower site to the park.

facts.status_note: The province's towers were decommissioned in 2015 and dismantled, per CBC News; no source describes this site today.
facts.agency: Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources

access.note: Nova Scotia Parks operates Valleyview with campsites and a look-off. No source says whether the former tower site is open or reachable.

events.note: Listed on a list of Nova Scotia DNR towers on the Maritimes Scanning Site, last updated September 18, 2009, at Valleyview Provincial Park, which says some listed towers are likely decommissioned.

corrections.current: Nova Scotia closed its fire towers in 2013 and had taken them down by 2015 (CBC News); no source says this one still stands.
corrections.proposed: The province's towers were decommissioned in 2015 and dismantled, per CBC News; no source describes this site today.
corrections.why: CBC News gives 2015 as the year of decommissioning, with dismantling after it. The 2013 date appears only in a 2012 provincial plan to replace 19 towers with aerial detection that year; the release does not record any tower coming down in 2013.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2012 provincial release set 2013 for replacing 19 towers with aerial detection, and 14 towers were to stay in remote areas. CBC News, carried by Yahoo, says the towers were decommissioned in 2015. The record uses the 2015 date because it reports the decommissioning itself; the 2012 release describes only a plan.

notes_for_editor: The 2009 list places a tower at Valleyview Prov Pk. with the tower name starred as tentative (DND*), so the name is uncertain; the story uses the park name only. The park page lists a 2026 operating season of June 5 to October 12, 2026, so these sources do not confirm the park is open now. No source ties the tower site to the park or describes its remains. The CBC original timed out in fetch_text and WebFetch returned 403, so the decommissioning claim is cited from the Yahoo copy. The brief's local_unit is 'Annapolis County', but STORY_GUIDE.md bars 'county' for a Canadian tower, so the story says 'the Annapolis area'; a human should confirm that wording.
